claim.value: Failure to meet the evidence threshold is not proof of no benefit.
claim.scope: A limit on interpreting a threshold failure; it does not assert that a benefit exists.

provenance.rationale: P028 explicitly states this limit and identifies circumstances that can leave effects unresolved.

signal_basis.value: The observed results fail to meet the predeclared minimum evidence threshold; small samples, sparse publications or censored accounts may leave effects unresolved.
signal_basis.scope: Interpretation of an evidence-threshold failure in the onboarding evaluation.

provenance.rationale: P009 supplies advance specification of the evidence threshold; P028 supplies threshold failure and the stated limitations on interpreting it.
The claim is supported without an unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: Failing an evidence threshold can reflect insufficient precision or incomplete observations even when a benefit exists. Threshold failure alone therefore does not establish absence of benefit, exactly within the claim's stated limits.
uncertainty: The threshold failure alone leaves whether a benefit exists unresolved.
